correctness.rationale: The exact population-loss convention and initial state are fixed. Away from \(\phi\in\pi\mathbb Z\) the Fourier spectrum is simple, and every eigenvector overlaps the sink, proving full decay. An integrated-density Lyapunov calculation gives the inverse-gap lifetime identity. In even order the index map \( (j,k)\mapsto(j-k,j+k) \) has two solutions on same-parity pairs, and cotangent multiplication yields the exact two-sector sum. Strict convexity in \(\sin^2(\phi/2)\) proves uniqueness modulo flux reversal, and AM-GM proves the independent rate optimum. At \(\phi=0,\pi\) degeneracies yield explicit accessible counts and nonzero dark mass. The embedded executable checker passed 168 spectral-gap identities, 150 full complex Lyapunov comparisons, 14 optimizer tests and 28 exceptional-energy counts. These tests are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A local-loss magnetic ring is a natural flux-control problem. The exact parity-sensitive spectral decomposition yields a complete all-even-size design rule for the global flux and absorber rate, disproves quarter flux as optimal in this model, quantifies the positive finite-size advantage and its asymptotic ratio, and distinguishes the two exceptional dark phases by both capture fraction and divergence coefficient. The nontrivial two-sector structure and exact optimizer are not arbitrary parameter substitutions, numerical enhancements or a generic inverse-gap restatement.
